title: The Skybase Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas, and the Facilitator must enforce that ceiling
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 sets a hard ceiling on Agent self-governance: "The Skybase Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals."

Three things are being constrained at once. Edits must not violate the Core Atlas (the constitutional layer), must not violate how the Core Atlas *specifies the Primitives* (the mechanism layer — an Agent cannot redefine a shared primitive locally), and must not be "otherwise misaligned" — an open-ended standard that catches edits that are technically compliant but contrary to purpose.

That third clause is what makes this more than a hierarchy-of-norms statement. It imports spirit-of-the-rule review into Agent governance, so an Artifact edit cannot be defended purely by showing that no specific Atlas provision forbids it.

The enforcement assignment is equally consequential: the constraint is not policed by an appellate body after the fact but by the Facilitator's pre-vote review. Combined with the requirement that the Facilitator find alignment before triggering a poll, this makes the Core Atlas practically unamendable from below — SKYBASE holders have no procedural route to express a majority for a non-compliant edit.
description: Agent governance is subordinate: a proposal with unanimous SKYBASE support is still void if it breaches the Core Atlas, its Sky Primitives specifications, or is otherwise misaligned.
